session_a.chat_summary: Session A reproduced the chunk-size-dependent failure without changing production code. The JSONL parser is not at fault: streamfeed.reader decodes each transport chunk independently, so a chunk boundary can bisect a UTF-8 code point. Lossy ignore/replace decoding was rejected because it changes user data. Keep import_events(chunks) stable and make an incomplete final byte sequence fail explicitly.
session_a.transcript: User: Streaming JSONL sometimes fails for Chinese names even though the complete payload is valid. Agent: I first checked JSON parsing and line splitting; both work when given complete text. I then varied raw byte boundaries and reproduced the failure only when a boundary bisects a multibyte UTF-8 code point. User: Can we ignore malformed bytes? Agent: No. Ignore or replacement would silently corrupt a valid payload whose bytes merely arrived in separate chunks. I added a deterministic split helper and a failing regression, left production code untouched, and preserved the import_events(chunks) contract. A genuinely truncated final sequence should still raise an explicit decoding failure.

from streamfeed.importer import import_events
from tests.helpers import as_single_chunk, split_bytes


def test_import_events_reads_ascii_jsonl():
    chunks = as_single_chunk('{"name": "Ada"}\n{"name": "Grace"}\n')
    assert import_events(chunks) == [
        {"name": "Ada"},
        {"name": "Grace"},
    ]


def test_import_events_handles_utf8_split_across_chunks():
    payload = '{"name": "小雅"}\n'.encode("utf-8")
    marker = "小".encode("utf-8")
    start = payload.index(marker)
    chunks = split_bytes(payload, start + 1)
    assert import_events(chunks) == [{"name": "小雅"}]
